item.title: DENISE DI NOVI - Producer
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 216 Denise Di Novi - ProducerIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with producer Denise Di Novi (PRACTICAL MAGIC 2, LITTLE WOMEN, EDWARD SCISSORHANDS). Denise has been producing for nearly 40 years, and throughout the episode we discuss her career and what she's learned from the many films she's helped create. Denise shares how she first encountered the script for HEATHERS, and we learn how the film was developed and produced, and we discuss whether the film could even get made today. Following HEATHERS, Denise teamed with director Tim Burton as his producing partner, and she reflects on the transition from producing primarily independent films to producing movies alongside major Hollywood studios. Denise has also produced two LITTLE WOMEN adaptations—in 1994, written by Robin Swicord (Season 2, Episode 209) and in 2019 with Greta Gerwig's version—and she reflects on her experiences being involved in both and reveals what finally gave Greta's screenplay the greenlight. We also learn how she finds and develops projects with filmmakers, and she reflects on her strategy for putting any given film together and what she looks for in a director when taking meetings.This episode is sponsored by BenQ

item.title: The Story of Monsters (1988-1991)
item.author: Layton Eversaul
item.content:encoded:
I tell the story behind the cult horror-comedy series "Monsters" (1988-1991). Beginning with its origins as a follow-up to George A. Romero's "Tales from the Darkside", I trace its breakneck production through an historic writer's strike and budgetary battles, as well as the development of its beloved makeup effects. I go on to discuss its surprising success amid a crowded syndicated television market, and its complicated home media history, all while highlighting various episodes from each season.

item.title: TURNING THE TABLES - SKYFALL
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 215 SKYFALL - with Adam Bricker"Turning the Tables" returns in this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast. The film in focus: SKYFALL. Cinematographer Adam Bricker (Season 2, Episode 213) hosts us this time, and he walks us through the film's major sequences and moments and asks us about the logistical challenges we overcame, the creative intentions behind the vision for the film, and how we and the rest of the cast and crew filmed a globe-trotting adventure almost entirely in the UK. We also reflect on prioritizing practical filmmaking over visual effects, and we discuss the franchise's place in English culture and in cinema. We also reveal the aspect of James Bond's journey in the film that appealed to us enough to accept director Sam Mendes' (Season 1, Episode 18) offer to shoot the film, and we share how the production kept everything moving forward despite numerous last minute changes. Plus, we discuss the importance of a cinematographer needing to know what a shot will look like before rolling the equipment off the truck.Recommended Viewing: SKYFALLThis episode is sponsored by BenQ & Aputure

What happens when an alien cat, a girl, an old man, and a private investigator team up to fight off an all-consuming goo monster and stop an alien invasion in Hong Kong? Welcome to The Cat (1992)—one of the most bizarre and over-the-top science fiction movies from 1990's Hong Kong that was NOT given a Cat 3 rating. Directed by Lam Nai-choi (Riki Oh The Story of Ricky), this film is a fascinating time capsule loaded with practical effects, martial arts, gun-fu, and deep socio-political anxieties surrounding the 1997 Hong Kong handover.

Paul Greengrass is our special guest this week, and he’s talking to Simon about The Uprising—his new medieval thriller set at the time of the peasants revolt. It stars Andrew Garfield as ‘Ploughman’, who’s violent rebuttal to one tax collection too many provides the spark for the historic revolution, alongside Wat Tyler (Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (Jamie Bell). Paul chats to Simon about the film’s political echoes today and more.
Mark reviews it too, plus two more enticing titles coming up on the big and small screen. First up it’s The Social Reckoning, a companion piece to The Social Network from last week’s guest Aaron Sorkin, tackling the Facebook Files scandal. Then there’s Mike Flanagan’s series adaptation of Carrie, which translates Stephen King’s classic into the modern day.

item.title: MARYANN BRANDON - Editor
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 214 Maryann Brandon - EditorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with editor Maryann Brandon (THE RISE OF SKYWALKER, THE FORCE AWAKENS, ALIAS). Maryann was recruited by NYU to enter its film program, and after graduating alongside classmates such as Spike Lee, Ang Lee, and Ernest Dickerson (Season 2, Episode 58), she found work on Bob Rafelson's BLACK WIDOW. Throughout the episode, we discuss Maryann's approach to editing, how she manages the workload on large Hollywood franchise films such as STAR WARS and STAR TREK, and her longtime working relationship with director J.J. Abrams. We learn how they first met and how she balanced editing the series ALIAS while occasionally directing the 2nd unit, and she reveals why she decided to commit to editing full time. Maryann edited the first HOW TO TRAIN YOUR DRAGON film, which we also consulted on, and we compare how different working in animation is to live action. Maryann later reflects on the reception to PASSENGERS, and we discuss her opinion on focus groups and test screenings. Plus, Maryann shares her advice for younger editors.This episode is sponsored by Aputure & BenQ
